summary: The social unit a room belongs to is now called a `unit`, not a `workspace`. `policy.toml`'s key changes with it, and a note discharge that had been addressing Honcho with a unit name now writes where recall reads.
details: **policy.toml: `workspace = "friends"` becomes `unit = "friends"`.** `_ConversationEntry` is `extra="forbid"`, so an un-edited file is a loud startup failure rather than rooms silently rejoining the default unit. The file and the image must move together.

Two unrelated things were both called `workspace`. Nora's own (DEC-105) is WHICH SOCIAL UNIT a room belongs to — the same people reachable in more than one place, which is what makes `send_to` between them something other than a leak. Honcho's is the first path segment of every memory call (`/v3/workspaces/{id}/...`): a TENANT, one per Nora, holding every unit at once. They sit at different levels and were never the same set, but they were spelled the same, and the resolver for each was called `workspace_for`.

**The defect that names the cost.** `NoteCurator._discharge` passed `note.workspace` as `conclude(workspace_id=...)`, so a person-claim discharged from a note in the `friends` unit was addressed to a Honcho workspace called `friends` — which does not exist — while `representation`/`chat` read the default and never looked there. On this deployment the same line also addressed `ridgeline`, a workspace that does exist and belongs to something else. The call now sends no `workspace_id`: one Nora is one Honcho workspace, and the unit scopes the note tier and nothing else.

Migration 0058 renames the column on `note`, `note_candidate`, `decision_log` and the fact tier's four tables, plus the two identifiers that spell the word (`idx_decision_log_workspace_ts`, `fact_entity_workspace_name_key`) and the six named NOT NULL constraints. Same type, same rows, no backfill.

design/24 §S.1's table already recorded this happening once before, with the word "group", and priced it at "a session's worth of confusion". `unit` is that section's own word for the thing. Honcho's spelling now survives only inside `nora/infra/honcho/`, and the compute sandbox's unrelated `workspace_root` is untouched.

**The granularity decision is reversed (operator, 2026-09-19).** One Nora is one Honcho workspace permanently; a second workspace means a second Nora, not a second unit. Honcho is multi-tenant — five workspaces on the deployed instance, read back live — but its peers are workspace-scoped, so a workspace per unit would split one person into N unrelated person-models and N self-cards with no way to split the derived history that already exists. `WorkspaceRouter`'s overrides map is now dead by decision rather than pending; design/24 §S.4 records what populating it would have cost.
limitations: **`search_memory_workspace` keeps its name and its model-facing description.** The whole verb moves in one piece later, because renaming a tool the model calls is a prompt change and is measured, not eyeballed. Until then the one tool in the roster spells the older word.

That verb's scope is also the open question this rename makes visible rather than answers: it searches Honcho's workspace `/search` with no `conversation_id`, so it reaches every unit, not just the caller's, and it filters against identity.toml's whole address book. That is now consistent with «one Nora, one workspace» — but it means the note tier is unit-isolated while the Honcho tier is not, and nothing states that as an accepted risk yet. design/24 §S.1's "safe by construction" bullet, which used to cover it, is struck.

Dashboards lose continuity on more than one series. Two carry the LABEL (`nora_note_curator_standing`, `nora_note_curator_bodies_read`) and one more is `nora_dream_home_room_missing_total`; four carry it as a label VALUE — `nora_relay_total{outcome="other_workspace"}` becomes `other_unit`, the note-candidate counter's `no_workspace`/`no_workspace_unavailable` and `refused_origin_wrong_workspace` follow, and the prefill stage `fire_workspace` becomes `fire_unit`. No declared-vs-incremented mismatch: the old spellings appear nowhere in `nora/`, `tests/` or `evals/` after the change. Retention is about four days, so the old series age out rather than needing a migration.
The eval corpora's `workspace:` key is now `unit:`. The values are unchanged and the key never reaches a prompt, so the suites grade the same cases; none of them was re-run for this change.
`release-fragments/released/` is left on the old word on purpose: those files record what past releases actually shipped.

The review of this branch found `search_memory_workspace` is registered on the TAG path in every room, not only the Dreamer's — which its own comment says is why its deployment-wide reach is acceptable. That is pre-existing and untouched here; this branch only makes the comments around it true. Tracked separately.
